Quick summary from runtime debugging (16:30–16:44 PT):
- Observed sudden token-bucket drain on the customer-global route for Acme (route id: acct-ACME-1872).
- A scheduled service-window change that was intended to increase burst allowance overnight had a misapplied policy: the change updated the global shared bucket cap instead of the per-customer burst override. The result: across-host traffic saw a hard cap drop from 10k TPS burst to 1k TPS during the service window.
- Requests above the new cap returned 429s from the inference gateway; internal queueing increased latency for allowed requests.
- We've reproduced the condition in a canary cluster by replaying a subset of their traffic pattern.

Mitigation plan in flight:
1) Roll-back the service-window policy change (15 min).
2) Temporarily enable a per-account emergency override to restore the prior burst allowance for acct-ACME-1872 (5 min after rollback).
3) Post-fix: run a policy audit and add a safety check to prevent global-cap writes without explicit per-account opt-out.

I'll execute the rollback now and will update you once the override is active.

- Marissa
